- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% of recent mean or 0.5–1.5 price points.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often over-optimistically continues upward; cap forecast slope or add 1–2 day lag correction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently under-anticipates drop; add 0.5–1.5 price point buffer below forecast.
- In high volatility regimes (e.g., 2022–2023), model underestimates mean reversion; apply 1–2 day smoothing or add 0.5–1.0 price point downward bias after 3–5 consecutive days of high sentiment.
- When sentiment shifts abruptly from negative to positive, model often fails to catch momentum; add 0.5–1.0 price point upward bias for first 2–3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5 price point upward bias for last 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.3) and price is trending, model often over-anticipates direction; use 0.5–1.0 price point buffer in either direction based on recent sentiment polarity.
